intake.question: How long have you been together?
What do you two argue about most?
What do you want from this reading?

options.label: To think about the long term

plan.title: How you love (and what you never say)
What your chemistry is made of
What you bring to the two of you
How you fight, and how you make up
What home feels like with you two

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. You love like you lead: full force, clear direction, your way.

Bom: You make them feel so safe.

Yeon: And sometimes a little steamrolled. "I booked it already" is romantic twice. The tenth time it's a policy.

Once this week, let them pick. The restaurant, the film, the plan. Then enjoy it out loud, even if it's not what you'd have chosen.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You love at full volume. Check if they can hear themselves think.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You love by tuning in: their mood, their week, what they need before they ask.

Yeon: And you put yourself last so smoothly nobody notices you did it.

Bom: Your needs aren't an inconvenience to the relationship. They're half of it.

This week, ask for one specific thing. Not "whatever you want". One thing you want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You give so gently. Let them give back.

strong.text: Strong charts fight to resolve and sometimes to win. Your energy can overwhelm a partner who needs time. Try a rule: whoever is calmer speaks second, and nobody makes a final decision in the first twenty minutes of an argument.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Cool first, decide later. Heat makes bad verdicts.

weak.text: Weak charts fight by retreating or giving in. It feels like keeping the peace; it often keeps the problem. Try writing your side down before the conversation, so the words are there even when your nerve isn't.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write your side down first. The words stay when your nerve goes.

strong.text: With a strong chart, you can drive the couple's growth: plans, goals, moves. Share the steering. Let your partner choose the next big adventure, even if it's not what you would have picked.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Hand over the steering wheel for the next adventure.

weak.text: With a weak chart, you may follow your partner's growth more than you lead your own. Pick one thing you want for yourself this year and ask your partner to support it. Couples grow best when both people do.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pick one thing for yourself this year. Ask for their support.

strong.text: A strong chart over decades can harden into habits that only one of you chose. Every few years, renegotiate the basics: who does what, where you live, how you spend holidays. It keeps the relationship belonging to both of you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Renegotiate the basics every few years. Fresh contract, same people.

weak.text: A weak chart over decades can quietly disappear into the relationship. Keep investing in yourself: friends, health, interests, ambitions. Your partner fell for a whole person; stay one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Keep your own friends, plans and dreams alive.

peer_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {dm_el}, your own element, the peer family: equals and rivals. In a couple you need equality. You want shared decisions, fair splits and a partner who stands beside you rather than above or below. You can turn competitive over small things, who's busier, who gave up more. The gift is that you never disappear into the relationship. The work is letting closeness feel like teamwork.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Equal partner energy. Just don't keep score of who's more tired.

output_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces, the output family: expression and play. You bring fun, creativity and affection to a relationship, the partner who makes ordinary days memorable. You may resist routine and rules at home. Bring the creativity into the routine: a playful ritual, a silly tradition, a weekly surprise.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your {heavy_el} makes home playful. Turn chores into a game.

wealth_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls, the wealth family: providing and managing. You show love by building a good life: a nice home, plans, security. Remember your partner also wants you, not just what you provide. Time together counts as much as everything you arrange.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Providing is love. So is sitting still with them for an hour.

power_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}, the power family: duty and standards. You're loyal, responsible and serious about commitment. You may hold your partner to standards they didn't agree to. Talk about expectations out loud; unspoken rules are the ones that get broken.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Say your expectations out loud. Unspoken rules get broken.

resource_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}, the resource family: comfort and understanding. You're a thoughtful, understanding partner, comfortable with quiet evenings and deep talks. You can wait too long to act on what you understand. Turn insight into gestures: if you know they need rest, book it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You know what they need. Do it before they ask.

output_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces: giving and expressing. In a couple you can pour out effort, affection and care until you're empty. Let your partner give back. Receiving gracefully is part of a balanced relationship.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Let them give back. Receiving is part of the deal.

wealth_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls, wealth heavy and self light: a lot to manage, little backup. In a couple you may carry the logistics, the finances, the family calendar, and feel exhausted. Split the load explicitly, on paper if needed.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Write down who does what. Then split it fairly.

power_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that presses on your {dm_el}: pressure and judgment. In a couple you can feel criticized easily and try very hard to be a good partner. Choose a partner who's warm, not harsh, and tell them that gentle feedback works best for you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for kindness in criticism. It's a fair request.

rooted_on_paper.text: In a relationship that looks like a partner who seems sure and steady and still needs reassurance more than anyone would guess. Both are true. Tell your partner which kind of reassurance helps, a hug, a message, a plan, so they don't have to guess.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Steady outside, needing reassurance inside. Say which kind helps.

output_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the output element, expression. You love in actions and may struggle with words. Your partner might need to hear it. One sentence a day about what you appreciate in them changes a lot.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Actions are lovely. Words too. One sentence a day.

wealth_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the wealth element, initiative in building a shared life. You're strong but may let practical plans drift. Pick one shared goal a year and make it concrete: a trip, a home project, a savings habit.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One concrete shared goal a year. Write it on the fridge.

power_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the power element, structure. You love freely and might forget the small commitments that make a partner feel secure. Keep the little promises: calling when late, remembering dates.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Call when you're running late. Every time. That's romance.

resource_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the resource element, being nurtured. You're strong and rarely let your partner take care of you. Let them. Being looked after is a gift to the person doing it too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Let them look after you. It's a gift for both.

output_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the output element, expression. It protects you from overgiving, and it can make your feelings hard to read. Small signs count: a hand on their arm, a note, a song you send.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A note, a touch, a song. Small signs carry a lot.

wealth_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the wealth element, initiative. You may let your partner drive the big decisions. Take the lead on one thing this year, a trip, a project, a new tradition.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You plan the next trip. Start to finish. Your call.

power_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the power element, outside pressure. Fewer rules weighing on you, which is nice. You may be unsure what's reasonable to ask of a partner. Respect, consistency and kindness are reasonable. Ask for them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Respect, consistency, kindness. Reasonable to ask for.

resource_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the resource element, support. You keep going on willpower. Make your partner part of your support system on purpose, and keep friends who refill you too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Let your partner into your refill routine.

none_strong.text: All five elements turn up in your pillars. For a strong chart that's range: you can be fun, steady, romantic and practical. The trap is assuming you can be everything for your partner. Let them be good at some things for you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can do it all. Let them be good at something for you.

none_weak.text: All five elements turn up in your pillars. For a weak chart that's flexibility: you adapt to almost any partner. Make sure adaptable doesn't mean invisible. Say your preference first sometimes.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Say your preference first sometimes. Flexible isn't invisible.

resource.title: What steadies you as a couple: {helper_el}
resource.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. For your weak {dm_el} chart it's {helper_el}, the element that feeds your Day Master. In a relationship that means being nurtured: a partner who looks after you, rest, and time with people who refill you. Love from a full cup, not an empty one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your refill is {helper_el}. Love from a full cup.

peer.title: What steadies you as a couple: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. Yours already has plenty of nourishment on paper, so what steadies you is your own element, {helper_el}. In a relationship that means friendship: a partner who is also your best friend, and friends who keep you grounded outside the couple.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your steadying element is {helper_el}: love that's also friendship.

output.title: What balances you as a couple: {helper_el}
output.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. A strong {dm_el} chart needs an outlet, and yours is {helper_el}, the element your Day Master produces. In a relationship that means play, expression and generosity. Spend your energy on fun together rather than on control.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your outlet is {helper_el}: fun together, not control.

wealth.title: What balances you as a couple: {helper_el}
wealth.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. Yours is strong and expressive, so what balances you is {helper_el}, the element your Day Master shapes. In a relationship that means building something concrete together: a home, a ritual, a shared project.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your balance is {helper_el}: build something together.

wood.text: Wood for a couple: walks in nature, growing plants together, learning something new side by side, long-term plans.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood for you two: walks, plants, learning side by side.

fire.text: Fire for a couple: warm evenings with friends, sunlight, celebrations, travel to bright places, laughing a lot.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fire for you two: friends, sunlight, celebrations.

earth.text: Earth for a couple: a cozy home, cooking together, routines, family meals, staying in on purpose.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth for you two: cozy home, cooking, staying in.

metal.text: Metal for a couple: clear agreements, a tidy shared space, honest talks, keeping promises precisely.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal for you two: clear agreements, kept precisely.

water.text: Water for a couple: deep conversations, quiet nights, time near water, giving each other space to think.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water for you two: deep talks and space to think.

rat.text: Your day branch is the Rat, 子, midnight Water, a peach-blossom branch linked with charm. In the spouse palace it means private intimacy matters most: late-night talks, inside jokes, a home where you can be fully yourself. You need a partner who respects your need for privacy and doesn't take your guardedness personally.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rat palace: inside jokes and late-night privacy.

ox.text: Your day branch is the Ox, 丑, cold Earth that stores Metal. In the spouse palace it means steadiness and devotion: you want a home that's solid and a partner who's in it for the long haul. You can be stubborn about how things are done at home. Pick your battles.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ox palace: devoted, and stubborn about the dishwasher.

tiger.text: Your day branch is the Tiger, 寅, early spring Wood. In the spouse palace it means independence and adventure: you need a partner who gives you freedom and joins you on spontaneous plans. A home that feels like a cage makes you restless.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tiger palace: freedom inside the commitment.

rabbit.text: Your day branch is the Rabbit, 卯, spring Wood, a peach-blossom branch. In the spouse palace it means tenderness and beauty: a gentle home, soft words, a partner who's kind. Harsh conflict at home hits you harder than most.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit palace: a gentle home, soft words.

dragon.text: Your day branch is the Dragon, 辰, damp Earth that stores Water. In the spouse palace it means a big inner life and big dreams for the relationship. You need a partner who takes your ambitions seriously and can handle some intensity.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon palace: big dreams for the two of you.

snake.text: Your day branch is the Snake, 巳, early summer Fire. In the spouse palace it means depth and loyalty with a private streak. You open up slowly and then completely. Trust is everything at home.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake palace: slow to open, then all in.

horse.text: Your day branch is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire, a peach-blossom branch. In the spouse palace it means passion and freedom: a warm, lively home and a partner who doesn't try to tie you down.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Horse palace: a warm, lively home with open doors.

goat.text: Your day branch is the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth. In the spouse palace it means gentleness and creativity: a cozy, artistic home and a partner who's kind and patient.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat palace: cozy, artistic, patient.

monkey.text: Your day branch is the Monkey, 申, early autumn Metal. In the spouse palace it means playfulness and intelligence: you need a partner who keeps you mentally stimulated and laughs at your jokes.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey palace: keep each other laughing.

rooster.text: Your day branch is the Rooster, 酉, autumn Metal, a peach-blossom branch. In the spouse palace it means refinement and order: a beautiful, tidy home and a partner who appreciates the details.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster palace: a beautiful, orderly home.

dog.text: Your day branch is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth that keeps Fire. In the spouse palace it means loyalty and protection: you're a devoted partner and need the same devotion back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Dog palace: devotion, given and needed.

pig.text: Your day branch is the Pig, 亥, early winter Water. In the spouse palace it means generosity and comfort: an easygoing, abundant home and a partner who enjoys simple pleasures with you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pig palace: abundance and simple pleasures.

new.text: You've been together under a year, the stage where you're still discovering each other's habits and the honeymoon glow is doing a lot of work. Use this reading as a map of what's coming: the patterns in the fighting chapter will show up eventually. Talk about them now, while it's still funny. Early on, you also set the tone for how you'll treat each other when tired or stressed. Be a little kinder than necessary on the bad days. It becomes the default.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Under a year: talk about the fight patterns while they're still funny.

settled.text: You've been together one to three years, the stage where routines set in and real differences show. This is when couples decide, often without noticing, how they'll handle conflict for the next decade. Pick your habits on purpose. This is also the time to agree on the big stuff: where you want to live, how you handle money, what weekends look like. Couples who talk about it now avoid fighting about it later.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One to three years: your fight habits are setting. Choose them.

long.text: You've been together three years or more. You know each other's patterns well, maybe too well. This reading might name things you've both felt for years. Use it to have one conversation you've been postponing. Long-term couples also benefit from novelty. Do one thing together this month you've never done before. It reminds both of you that there's still more to find out.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Three years plus: have the conversation you've been postponing.

committed.text: You're engaged or married, in it for the long run. The long-term chapter matters most for you. Saju sees marriage as two charts sharing a home; the day branch chapter is your household weather report. Marriage or engagement also brings families into the picture. Talk about how you'll handle holidays and in-laws before the next big one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Engaged or married: the home chapter is your weather report.

unsaid.text: You didn't say how long you've been together. However long it is, the patterns in this reading are the ones that shape your days. Read it together and see which parts make you both laugh. Then pick one chapter each to discuss over dinner. It's a better conversation starter than asking how their day was.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Couch, two phones, this reading. Argue about the details.

time.text: You mostly argue about time and attention. Underneath, that's usually about feeling prioritized. Agree on one protected ritual, a weekly dinner, a phone-free hour, that nothing interrupts. Also notice how each of you shows love with time: some people want long stretches together, others want many small check-ins. Neither is wrong; they just need translating.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fights about time are fights about priority. Protect one ritual.

logistics.text: You mostly argue about chores, plans and money stuff. These fights are rarely about the dishes; they're about fairness and feeling respected. Write down who does what and review it every few months. And celebrate when things go smoothly. Couples rarely thank each other for taking out the trash, and it costs nothing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: It's never the dishes. It's fairness. Write the list.

feelings.text: You mostly argue about feelings and communication: who said what, how it sounded, what wasn't said. Try a simple rule: repeat back what you heard before you answer. Half of these fights end right there. It also helps to agree on a pause word, something silly either of you can say when a conversation is getting too hot. Twenty minutes apart, then back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mirror their words first. Then answer.

people.text: You mostly argue about friends or family. These fights are about loyalty: whose side you're on. Agree that in front of others you're a team, and have the disagreement privately later. Set a few boundaries together for how often you see each other's families and friends. Clear agreements beat case-by-case negotiations.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: In public, a team. Disagree privately later.

unsaid.text: No fight topic chosen. Every couple has a favorite topic. Notice yours this month; it usually points to what each of you needs most. Whatever it is, fights are information. They show where each of you feels unseen.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Notice your favorite fight topic. It points to a need.

understand.text: You want to understand them better. Go back to the chapter about who they are and read it out loud to them. Ask which parts are true. Their answers will teach you more than the chart. Then do the same for yours: let them read your chapters and tell you which parts they recognize. You might learn how you look from the outside.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Read their chapter out loud to them. Ask what's true.

fight.text: You want to fight less. Pick one tip from the fighting chapter and agree to try it for a month. One change, practiced, beats ten good intentions. Also try ending every argument with one thing you appreciate about each other. It sounds cheesy. It works.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One fighting tip, one month, both of you.

future.text: You want to think about the long term. Take the growing and long-run chapters as a starting point for a conversation about the next five years: where, how, with what. Write it down and revisit it next year. Include the fun parts too: trips, hobbies, dreams. Long-term planning isn't only mortgages.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Talk about the next five years. Write it down.

fun.text: You're just curious. Perfect. Read the spicy parts out loud and argue about which of you is more stubborn. Then compare reading codes with friends' couples and decide whose pairing would win a reality show.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Just curious? Argue about who's more stubborn.

unsaid.text: No goal picked for this reading. Maybe you'll know by the end. Pick the one sentence that stung or made you smile, and tell your partner. The best readings start conversations. This one has done its job if you talk about it tonight.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Share the line that hit hardest. That's the conversation.

wood.heading: What you need from love: to feel it growing
wood.text:
Yeon: You don't need fireworks. You need a direction. A trip on the calendar. A "next year we should".

Bom: Standing still scares you more than fighting.

Yeon: Which is why you start "where is this going" talks at completely random moments. Like during dessert.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Talk about your future together. It calms you more than you admit.

fire.heading: What you need from love: to feel lit up
fire.text:
Bom: You need warmth you can see. Eye contact. Excitement. Them lighting up when you walk in.

Yeon: If they say "nice" in a flat voice about something you're thrilled about, you'll think about it for a week.

Bom: Ask them to show it. Out loud. It's allowed.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "Nice." The most dangerous word you can say to a Fire person.

earth.heading: What you need from love: to feel safe
earth.text:
Bom: You need steadiness. Same person on Tuesday as on Saturday. Plans that actually happen.

Yeon: Last-minute cancellations hit you harder than any fight.

Bom: Tell them that. "Consistency is how I feel loved" is a full sentence.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Consistency is your love language. Say it out loud once.

metal.heading: What you need from love: to feel respected
metal.text:
Yeon: You need respect before romance. Keep your word, and you're theirs forever. Break it once, and you'll remember the date.

Bom: You show love by being reliable. You need it back the same way.

Yeon: Also, you want to be taken seriously. Laugh at the wrong moment and you'll go very, very quiet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can forgive a lot. A broken promise goes in the permanent file.

water.heading: What you need from love: to feel understood
water.text:
Bom: You need someone who gets the layers. Not just what you said. What you meant.

Yeon: You'll test it, too. A vague "I'm fine" to see if they notice it wasn't.

Bom: Try saying the actual thing. Being understood is easier when you're also being clear.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "I'm fine" is not a puzzle they signed up to solve.

gap-wood.heading: Their soul
gap-wood.text:
Your partner is Gap Wood, the tall pine. They love with structure and loyalty: plans, promises kept, a sense that the relationship is going somewhere. They're protective and principled, and they show love by being dependable more than by being poetic. What they need from you is respect for their principles and the occasional reminder that they don't have to carry everything. What they rarely say: they'd love to be the one cared for, for once.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

eul-wood.heading: Their soul
eul-wood.text:
Your partner is Eul Wood, the climbing flower. They love through closeness and attention: small daily messages, remembering details, weaving you into their world. They're adaptable and charming, and they avoid open conflict. What they need from you is consistent reassurance that they're chosen, and direct words, because they'll read every hint. What they rarely say: they sometimes bend too far to keep the peace.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

byeong-fire.heading: Their soul
byeong-fire.text:
Your partner is Byeong Fire, the sun. They love warmly, loudly and generously: surprises, adventures, public affection. They're optimistic and quick to forgive, and they flare up fast when hurt. What they need from you is visible appreciation and some enthusiasm back; lukewarm makes them anxious. What they rarely say: their brightness needs refueling, and they want to be celebrated too.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

jeong-fire.heading: Their soul
jeong-fire.text:
Your partner is Jeong Fire, the candle. They love quietly and deeply: attention, emotional intimacy, remembering what matters to you. They're perceptive and caring, and when hurt they go quiet rather than loud. What they need from you is emotional safety and you asking how they are, then waiting for the real answer. What they rarely say: they're giving more than they show, and they'd love to be looked after.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

mu-earth.heading: Their soul
mu-earth.text:
Your partner is Mu Earth, the mountain. They love through stability: showing up, solving problems, building a safe life. They're loyal and patient, not very verbal about feelings, and hard to move once decided. What they need from you is appreciation for their steadiness and patience when they need time to process. What they rarely say: they get lonely when nobody asks how they really are.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

gi-earth.heading: Their soul
gi-earth.text:
Your partner is Gi Earth, the garden field. They love by tending: meals, reminders, routines, quietly making your life easier. They're caring and practical, and they absorb conflict until it overflows. What they need from you is noticing the care out loud and sharing the load. What they rarely say: they worry about being enough, and they need tending too.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

gyeong-metal.heading: Their soul
gyeong-metal.text:
Your partner is Gyeong Metal, the sword. They love through loyalty, honesty and protection. They're direct, brave and fiercely committed, and their honesty can cut. What they need from you is directness back, no hints, and gentleness when they finally show their soft side. What they rarely say: the armor is heavy, and they'd love a safe place to put it down.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

sin-metal.heading: Their soul
sin-metal.text:
Your partner is Sin Metal, the jewel. They love with thoughtfulness and refinement: careful gifts, chosen words, beautiful moments. They're sensitive and selective, and when hurt they go cool rather than loud. What they need from you is consideration, respect and sincere compliments. What they rarely say: careless comments scratch them more deeply than you'd guess.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

im-water.heading: Their soul
im-water.text:
Your partner is Im Water, the ocean. They love with depth, curiosity and a hunger for shared adventures. They need freedom and pull away from possessiveness, and when upset they drift rather than fight. What they need from you is space plus a steady presence they can return to. What they rarely say: they want a harbor more than they admit.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

gye-water.heading: Their soul
gye-water.text:
Your partner is Gye Water, the rain. They love with intuition and gentleness: comfort, understanding, emotional attunement. They absorb your moods and retreat when hurt, often saying they're fine when they're not. What they need from you is kindness, reassurance and direct questions about how they feel. What they rarely say: they sometimes lose themselves in the relationship and need you to help them stay whole.

Living with this soul day to day, you'll notice their rhythm: what they do when they're stressed, how they recharge, what they need after a long week. Watch for those patterns for a month and adjust one small thing for them. Nothing says 'I see you' like changing your habits without being asked.

strong.heading: Their chart
strong.text: Their chart is well backed: their Day Master gets plenty of support from their season and pillars. Expect a partner who knows their own mind and has the energy to go after what they want. They're easy to lean on. They can also forget to ask what you think. Tell them, early and plainly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Their chart is well backed. Tell them what you think, early.

weak.heading: Their chart
weak.text: Their chart leans light: their Day Master gets less support from their season and pillars. In a relationship that usually means a partner who's sensitive, adaptable and quick to read the room. They give a lot and may not ask for much. Check in on what they want; they'll often say 'whatever you like' and mean the opposite.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Their chart leans light. 'Whatever you like' might not be true.

spring.heading: Their season
spring.text:
They were born in spring, the season of beginnings. In love they tend to be hopeful, energetic and drawn to new experiences. They bring freshness. They also get restless if the relationship stops growing. Keep starting things together.

Seasons also show when someone feels most like themselves. Plan something special for them in their birth season; it tends to land well.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Spring-born partner: keep starting new things together.

summer.heading: Their season
summer.text:
They were born in summer, the season of full heat. In love they tend to be passionate, expressive and social. They bring warmth and fun. They can burn out or flare up quickly. Give them room to cool down.

Seasons also show when someone feels most like themselves. Plan something special for them in their birth season; it tends to land well.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Summer-born partner: warm, expressive, needs cooling-off time.

autumn.heading: Their season
autumn.text:
They were born in autumn, the season of harvest and clarity. In love they tend to be discerning, loyal and practical. They know what they want. They can seem critical when they're really just being precise. Ask what they mean before you take it personally.

Seasons also show when someone feels most like themselves. Plan something special for them in their birth season; it tends to land well.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Autumn-born partner: precise, not critical. Usually.

winter.heading: Their season
winter.text:
They were born in winter, the season of stillness and depth. In love they tend to be thoughtful, private and deep. They warm up slowly and then completely. Be patient with their quiet; it's not distance.

Seasons also show when someone feels most like themselves. Plan something special for them in their birth season; it tends to land well.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter-born partner: quiet isn't distance. Be patient.

earth.heading: Their season
earth.text:
They were born in the Earth days between seasons. In love they tend to be steady, adaptable and good at transitions. They're the calm one when life changes. Lean on that, and make sure they get to lean too.

Seasons also show when someone feels most like themselves. Plan something special for them in their birth season; it tends to land well.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Earth-days partner: the calm in changes. Let them lean too.

0.heading: What they are to you: the Friend (比肩)
0.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Friend, 比肩: same element as you, same polarity. You're mirror souls, equals who understand each other's instincts without explanation. The chemistry is companionship, like a best friend you also happen to love. You'll rarely feel misunderstood. The challenge is that mirrors double everything: shared strengths and shared blind spots. If you're both stubborn, nobody bends. Agree in advance who decides what, and bring in friends who think differently.

In daily life, this looks like shared taste: you like the same jokes, want the same kind of weekend, and decide things quickly. Friends may say you're like an old married couple even early on. The danger appears when you both want the same thing at the same time, the last slice, the window seat, the final word, and neither of you is used to yielding. Practice generosity in small, silly ways. Being equals means sometimes choosing to come second.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mirror souls. You get each other without explaining.

1.heading: What they are to you: the Rival Sibling (劫財)
1.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Rob Wealth, 劫財: same element as you, opposite polarity. Think sibling energy with a crush on top: playful, competitive, very alive. You push each other, tease each other and get better because the other one is watching. The risk is competition sneaking into the relationship, who's right, who's more tired, who sacrificed more. Turn the rivalry outward: be a team against the world, not opponents in the kitchen.

In daily life, this looks like banter: you challenge each other's opinions, compete at games, and keep each other sharp. It's very attractive and very tiring if it never switches off. Build in moments of pure softness, no teasing, no debate. Rivals become partners the moment one of you says 'you were right' without irony.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Sibling-rival chemistry. Fun, as long as you're on the same team.

2.heading: What they are to you: the Joy (食神)
2.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Eating God, 食神: your element feeds theirs, same polarity. You nurture them naturally, and it doesn't feel like work. You make them laugh, cook for them, encourage them, and they bloom around you. The chemistry is easy, warm and playful. The risk is imbalance: you giving, them receiving, until you notice your cup is empty. Make sure the care comes back your way.

In daily life, this looks like you cooking, planning, encouraging, and them glowing. It's lovely to give where it lands so well. Over years, you need to receive too, or your joy in giving turns into quiet fatigue. Ask for one specific thing a week. They'll likely be thrilled to finally know what you want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You feed them joy without trying. Let some come back.

3.heading: What they are to you: the Spark (傷官)
3.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Hurting Officer, 傷官: your element feeds theirs, opposite polarity. You bring out their expressive, rebellious, creative side, and they bring out your honesty. The chemistry is electric and talkative, full of opinions. The risk is criticism: you see exactly how they could be better and you may say so too often. Praise twice as much as you correct.

In daily life, this looks like lively conversations, honest feedback and a partner who's more themselves around you. You bring out their edge, and they bring out your wit. Keep the honesty kind. The same sentence can be a gift or a cut depending on tone, timing and whether it's the fourth note of the day.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Electric and opinionated. Praise twice as often as you critique.

4.heading: What they are to you: the Adventure (偏財)
4.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Indirect Wealth, 偏財: your element shapes theirs, same polarity. They're exciting to you, a little unpredictable, the person who makes life feel bigger. The chemistry is attraction and adventure: travel, spontaneity, fun. The risk is treating the relationship like a conquest that's finished once won. Keep courting them long after the chase is over.

In daily life, this looks like spontaneity: last-minute plans, new restaurants, a partner who makes ordinary weeks feel like an adventure. The early chase was thrilling. The long game is choosing them again and again once they're yours. Plan surprises even after years.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They make life feel bigger. Keep courting after the chase.

5.heading: What they are to you: the Partner (正財)
5.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Direct Wealth, 正財: your element shapes theirs, opposite polarity. Classically this is the steady partner, the person you build a life with. The chemistry is practical, loyal and grounded: shared plans, a home, a future with dates in it. The risk is routine replacing romance. Schedule the romance like you schedule everything else.

In daily life, this looks like shared plans, budgets, homes and a steady rhythm. You make each other's lives work. The danger is becoming excellent roommates who forget to flirt. Keep one evening a week that has nothing to do with logistics.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The build-a-life partner. Put romance in the calendar.

6.heading: What they are to you: the Challenge (七殺)
6.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Seven Killings, 七殺: their element presses on yours, same polarity. It's the most intense of the ten roles. They challenge you, push you and pull you in magnetically. You grow fast with them and you sometimes feel overpowered. The chemistry is passion with pressure. The work is setting boundaries and making sure the intensity stays respectful.

In daily life, this looks like big feelings, strong opinions and growth that comes fast because you push each other. Passion is high and so is friction. Agree on how you'll fight before you fight, and remember that intensity only feels good when both people feel safe.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Intense and magnetic. Keep the intensity respectful.

7.heading: What they are to you: the Anchor (正官)
7.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Direct Officer, 正官: their element shapes yours, opposite polarity. Classically this is the respected partner: they bring structure, stability and a sense of doing things properly. You feel safer and more organized with them. The risk is feeling judged or constrained. Say when you need flexibility; good anchors give the rope some slack.

In daily life, this looks like order and mutual respect: shared standards, reliable plans, a partner who makes you feel taken seriously. You may feel a little more grown-up around them. Make sure that doesn't turn into feeling watched. Keep some play in the structure.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They steady you. Ask for slack when the rope's too tight.

8.heading: What they are to you: the Mystic (偏印)
8.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Indirect Resource, 偏印: their element feeds yours, same polarity. They support you in unusual ways: deep understanding, unconventional advice, a sense that they see the strange parts of you and like them. The chemistry is intuitive and quiet. The risk is drifting into your own worlds. Plan shared things, not only shared silences.

In daily life, this looks like long talks about unusual things, comfortable silences and a shared private world nobody else quite understands. Lovely, as long as you also step out into the world together. Plan trips, parties, projects, so the quiet stays a choice.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They understand your strange parts. Plan shared adventures too.

9.heading: What they are to you: the Nurturer (正印)
9.text:
In saju's ten roles, {them} is your Direct Resource, 正印: their element feeds yours, opposite polarity. They nurture you: safety, encouragement, the feeling of coming home. You relax around them in a way you don't elsewhere. The risk is depending on them so much that you stop growing on your own. Let their care be a base, not a bubble.

In daily life, this looks like comfort: they look after you, and you feel safe enough to rest. It's precious. Make sure you also look after them, and keep growing on your own, so the relationship stays a home you return to rather than a place you hide.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Home base, not a hiding place. Keep growing out there.

combo.heading: Your two stems: a heavenly combination
combo.text:
Your two Day Masters form one of saju's five heavenly combinations (天干合), pairs of stems that naturally bind. It's the classic sign of strong attraction and a feeling of fitting together. You may have felt it early. A combination is a pull, not a guarantee: it makes connection easy and still asks both of you to do the ordinary work.

Classically, combined stems describe a couple who naturally move toward each other, even after distance. Treat it as encouragement, not a promise: the pull makes reconciliation easier, which means the habit of repairing quickly matters even more for you two.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A heavenly combination. The pull is real. The work still counts.

same_stem.heading: Your two stems: the same stem
same_stem.text:
You share the exact same Day Master. Saju sees this as deep familiarity: you think alike, react alike and understand each other quickly. The risk is that nobody balances anyone. Find your differences on purpose and value them, because they're where the growth is.

Same-stem couples tend to amplify each other's moods. When one of you is excited, both are. When one is low, both sink. Agree on a small rescue ritual for low days, a walk, a favorite meal, a film, so one of you can pull the other up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same stem. Find your differences on purpose.

same_element.heading: Your two stems: same element, different polarity
same_element.text:
Your Day Masters share an element with opposite polarity, one yang and one yin version. You understand each other's core and express it differently, one louder, one softer. It balances nicely. Respect the other's style instead of trying to convert it.

In practice, the yang one of you usually takes the lead in public and the yin one in private. Lean into that. It's a natural division of labor that keeps either of you from carrying everything.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same element, different volume. Respect the other style.

generating.heading: Your two stems: a generating pair
generating.text:
One of your elements feeds the other in saju's generating cycle. It's a supportive pairing: one gives, one grows. Couples like this feel nourishing. Watch that the giving doesn't flow only one way for too long.

In practice, notice which of you is the feeder and which is the fed. Then, deliberately, swap roles now and then. The one who usually gives needs to be given to, and the one who usually receives grows by giving.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One feeds the other. Check the flow goes both ways sometimes.

controlling.heading: Your two stems: a controlling pair
controlling.text:
One of your elements checks the other in saju's controlling cycle. It brings friction and also structure: you sharpen each other, notice each other's flaws and push each other to grow. It works best with explicit respect and a sense of humor.

In practice, controlling pairs do well with clear roles: who decides what, who has the final say on which topics. Friction drops when the boundaries are drawn in advance.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You sharpen each other. Respect and humor keep it sweet.

clash.heading: Your two stems: a clash
clash.text:
Your Day Masters are a classic stem clash, two strong energies facing each other directly. It brings passion, debate and some fireworks. Clash couples can be dynamic and long-lasting when they agree on a few ground rules for arguments and never fight dirty.

In practice, clash couples are rarely bored. Use the energy: plan challenges together, debate ideas, push each other's ambitions. Direct the clash outward and it becomes a strength.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Stem clash. Fireworks. Set ground rules for arguments.

peer.heading: When your elements argue
peer.text:
You and {them} share an element, so your fights are fights between equals: two people who both think they're right, in similar ways. Arguments can become standoffs. The way out is letting one person win small things on purpose, and taking turns.

Every pairing of elements has its own fight script. Knowing yours means you can catch it in the first minute instead of the twentieth. Next time an argument starts, name the pattern out loud, half joking: 'Here we go, the usual.' It often breaks the spell.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Equal fighters. Take turns winning the small ones.

output.heading: When your elements argue
output.text:
Your element feeds {them_el}, theirs. In fights you tend to explain, advise and pour out words, and they can feel lectured. Ask one question for every point you make. You'll find out what they're actually upset about.

Every pairing of elements has its own fight script. Knowing yours means you can catch it in the first minute instead of the twentieth. Next time an argument starts, name the pattern out loud, half joking: 'Here we go, the usual.' It often breaks the spell.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fewer lectures, more questions. Find the real hurt.

wealth.heading: When your elements argue
wealth.text:
Your element controls {them_el}, theirs. In fights you can try to manage them, fix the problem, decide the solution. They may feel controlled. Ask what they need before you offer a fix.

Every pairing of elements has its own fight script. Knowing yours means you can catch it in the first minute instead of the twentieth. Next time an argument starts, name the pattern out loud, half joking: 'Here we go, the usual.' It often breaks the spell.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ask what they need before fixing anything.

power.heading: When your elements argue
power.text:
{them_el}, their element, controls yours. In fights you may feel pressured, criticized or overruled, and either fight back hard or shut down. Say 'I feel pushed' early. It's information, not weakness, and it changes their tone.

Every pairing of elements has its own fight script. Knowing yours means you can catch it in the first minute instead of the twentieth. Next time an argument starts, name the pattern out loud, half joking: 'Here we go, the usual.' It often breaks the spell.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: 'I feel pushed.' Say it early. It changes the tone.

resource.heading: When your elements argue
resource.text:
{them_el}, their element, feeds yours. In fights they often end up comforting you, even when they're the one who's upset. Notice that. Make space for their hurt too, before yours.

Every pairing of elements has its own fight script. Knowing yours means you can catch it in the first minute instead of the twentieth. Next time an argument starts, name the pattern out loud, half joking: 'Here we go, the usual.' It often breaks the spell.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They comfort you even mid-fight. Ask about their hurt first.

rat.heading: Your spouse palace: the Rat
rat.text:
Your day branch is the Rat, 子, midnight Water, a peach-blossom branch linked with charm. In the spouse palace it means private intimacy matters most: late-night talks, inside jokes, a home where you can be fully yourself. You need a partner who respects your need for privacy and doesn't take your guardedness personally.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rat palace: inside jokes and late-night privacy.

ox.heading: Your spouse palace: the Ox
ox.text:
Your day branch is the Ox, 丑, cold Earth that stores Metal. In the spouse palace it means steadiness and devotion: you want a home that's solid and a partner who's in it for the long haul. You can be stubborn about how things are done at home. Pick your battles.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ox palace: devoted, and stubborn about the dishwasher.

tiger.heading: Your spouse palace: the Tiger
tiger.text:
Your day branch is the Tiger, 寅, early spring Wood. In the spouse palace it means independence and adventure: you need a partner who gives you freedom and joins you on spontaneous plans. A home that feels like a cage makes you restless.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tiger palace: freedom inside the commitment.

rabbit.heading: Your spouse palace: the Rabbit
rabbit.text:
Your day branch is the Rabbit, 卯, spring Wood, a peach-blossom branch. In the spouse palace it means tenderness and beauty: a gentle home, soft words, a partner who's kind. Harsh conflict at home hits you harder than most.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit palace: a gentle home, soft words.

dragon.heading: Your spouse palace: the Dragon
dragon.text:
Your day branch is the Dragon, 辰, damp Earth that stores Water. In the spouse palace it means a big inner life and big dreams for the relationship. You need a partner who takes your ambitions seriously and can handle some intensity.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon palace: big dreams for the two of you.

snake.heading: Your spouse palace: the Snake
snake.text:
Your day branch is the Snake, 巳, early summer Fire. In the spouse palace it means depth and loyalty with a private streak. You open up slowly and then completely. Trust is everything at home.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake palace: slow to open, then all in.

horse.heading: Your spouse palace: the Horse
horse.text:
Your day branch is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire, a peach-blossom branch. In the spouse palace it means passion and freedom: a warm, lively home and a partner who doesn't try to tie you down.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Horse palace: a warm, lively home with open doors.

goat.heading: Your spouse palace: the Goat
goat.text:
Your day branch is the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth. In the spouse palace it means gentleness and creativity: a cozy, artistic home and a partner who's kind and patient.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat palace: cozy, artistic, patient.

monkey.heading: Your spouse palace: the Monkey
monkey.text:
Your day branch is the Monkey, 申, early autumn Metal. In the spouse palace it means playfulness and intelligence: you need a partner who keeps you mentally stimulated and laughs at your jokes.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey palace: keep each other laughing.

rooster.heading: Your spouse palace: the Rooster
rooster.text:
Your day branch is the Rooster, 酉, autumn Metal, a peach-blossom branch. In the spouse palace it means refinement and order: a beautiful, tidy home and a partner who appreciates the details.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster palace: a beautiful, orderly home.

dog.heading: Your spouse palace: the Dog
dog.text:
Your day branch is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth that keeps Fire. In the spouse palace it means loyalty and protection: you're a devoted partner and need the same devotion back.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Dog palace: devotion, given and needed.

pig.heading: Your spouse palace: the Pig
pig.text:
Your day branch is the Pig, 亥, early winter Water. In the spouse palace it means generosity and comfort: an easygoing, abundant home and a partner who enjoys simple pleasures with you.

That's your side of the household. Your partner brings their own palace, and the section below says how the two meet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pig palace: abundance and simple pleasures.

same.heading: Your day branches together
same.text:
You share the same day branch. Your spouse palaces mirror each other, so you want the same things from home, in similar ways. Easy to live together, and easy to fall into the same ruts. Shake up routines together now and then.

Your day branches describe what living together feels like at the level of mornings, chores and weekends. These small rhythms decide how happy a couple feels more than any big gesture does.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same spouse palace. Easy living. Shake up the routines.

clash.heading: Your day branches together
clash.text:
Your day branches clash, the opposite animals of the zodiac. Saju reads this as friction in daily life: different rhythms, different ideas about home. It's not a dealbreaker, it's homework. Agree on the household basics explicitly and give each other space when the rhythms collide.

Your day branches describe what living together feels like at the level of mornings, chores and weekends. These small rhythms decide how happy a couple feels more than any big gesture does.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Clashing palaces. Agree on household basics out loud.

harmony.heading: Your day branches together
harmony.text:
Your day branches are in six-harmony (六合), a pair that naturally combines. Saju reads this as ease in daily life together: living with each other feels natural, and small habits fit. A real gift. Don't take it for granted.

Your day branches describe what living together feels like at the level of mornings, chores and weekends. These small rhythms decide how happy a couple feels more than any big gesture does.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Six-harmony palaces. Daily life fits. Treasure it.

trio.heading: Your day branches together
trio.text:
Your day branches belong to the same three-harmony group (三合), animals that share an element. Saju reads this as teamwork at home: you pull in the same direction and support each other's goals.

Your day branches describe what living together feels like at the level of mornings, chores and weekends. These small rhythms decide how happy a couple feels more than any big gesture does.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Three-harmony palaces. Teamwork at home.

neutral.heading: Your day branches together
neutral.text:
Your day branches are neutral with each other, neither combining nor clashing. Home life will feel like what you make of it. Build your own rituals on purpose; nothing in the chart builds them for you.

Your day branches describe what living together feels like at the level of mornings, chores and weekends. These small rhythms decide how happy a couple feels more than any big gesture does.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Neutral palaces. Build your rituals on purpose.

strong_strong.heading: You two, by chart strength
strong_strong.text:
Both of your charts are well backed. Two people with firm opinions and plenty of energy: a power couple when aligned, a standoff when not. Decide together who leads which area of life, and stick to it.

Chart strength isn't about who's better. It's about who naturally takes up more space and who naturally makes room. Healthy couples notice the pattern and balance it on purpose.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two well-backed charts. Divide the areas you each lead.

strong_weak.heading: You two, by chart strength
strong_weak.text:
Your chart is the well-backed one and theirs leans light. You naturally lead, they naturally adapt. It can be harmonious, or you can steamroll without noticing. Ask their opinion first on decisions that affect both of you.

Chart strength isn't about who's better. It's about who naturally takes up more space and who naturally makes room. Healthy couples notice the pattern and balance it on purpose.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You lead, they adapt. Ask their opinion first.

weak_strong.heading: You two, by chart strength
weak_strong.text:
Their chart is the well-backed one and yours leans light. They naturally lead, you naturally adapt. That can feel safe, or you can slowly disappear. Keep stating your preferences, even small ones.

Chart strength isn't about who's better. It's about who naturally takes up more space and who naturally makes room. Healthy couples notice the pattern and balance it on purpose.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They lead, you adapt. Keep stating your preferences.

weak_weak.heading: You two, by chart strength
weak_weak.text:
Both of your charts lean light. You're both sensitive and considerate, which makes home gentle, and decisions slow. Take turns being the one who decides, so the restaurant gets chosen before you're both starving.

Chart strength isn't about who's better. It's about who naturally takes up more space and who naturally makes room. Healthy couples notice the pattern and balance it on purpose.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Two gentle charts. Take turns deciding dinner.

yang.heading: Your yang side in love
yang.text: Your Day Master is yang, the outward half. In a couple you tend to initiate: suggesting plans, raising issues, moving things forward. Growth happens when you also leave space for your partner's initiative.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Yang in love: you initiate. Leave room for theirs.

yin.heading: Your yin side in love
yin.text: Your Day Master is yin, the inward half. In a couple you tend to deepen rather than initiate: reflecting, adjusting, understanding. Growth happens when you also start things yourself.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Yin in love: you deepen. Start something yourself too.

wood.heading: What their element brings you
wood.text: Their Day Master is Wood, and Wood brings growth into a relationship. With them, life tends to move forward: plans, ambitions, a sense that the two of you are going somewhere. They'll encourage your goals and expect you to have some. On tired days that can feel like pressure. On good days it feels like being believed in. Tell them which goals are yours and which ones you're happy to leave as dreams.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A Wood partner believes in where you're going. Name your goals.

fire.heading: What their element brings you
fire.text: Their Day Master is Fire, and Fire brings warmth and visibility. With them, you get celebrated: birthdays matter, wins get toasted, friends get invited over. They make the relationship feel alive and public. They also need warmth back, and they notice when it's missing. A compliment, a laugh at their joke, a visible thank-you keeps their flame high.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A Fire partner celebrates you loudly. Applaud back.

earth.heading: What their element brings you
earth.text: Their Day Master is Earth, and Earth brings steadiness. With them, there's ground under your feet: routines, a home that works, someone who stays calm when things go wrong. They're the one who remembers to buy milk and to call your mother on her birthday. Notice it and name it. Earth people rarely ask for credit and quietly wish for it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: An Earth partner is your ground. Say thank you for the milk.

metal.heading: What their element brings you
metal.text: Their Day Master is Metal, and Metal brings clarity and loyalty. With them, you always know where you stand. They'll tell you the truth about the haircut, the job offer and the friend who isn't treating you well. That honesty is a form of protection. Receive it as care, and ask them to soften the delivery when you need it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A Metal partner tells you the truth. It's protection, mostly.

water.heading: What their element brings you
water.text: Their Day Master is Water, and Water brings depth and perspective. With them, conversations go further, ideas get bigger, and you see your own life from new angles. They need space to think and won't always explain where their mind went. Ask. They love being asked, and you'll get the best conversations of your life.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A Water partner deepens everything. Ask where their mind went.

spring.heading: Your season at home
spring.text: Born in spring, you bring fresh starts to a shared home: rearranged furniture, new plants, sudden plans to repaint the bedroom. You get restless when home life stops changing. Agree on small yearly refreshes so you don't have to move house to feel new.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Spring at home: a yearly refresh, not a new address.

summer.heading: Your season at home
summer.text: Born in summer, you want a lively home: friends over, music on, doors open. A quiet partner may need you to protect some evenings for just the two of you. Balance the party house with a few sacred nights in.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Summer at home: party house, plus sacred nights in.

autumn.heading: Your season at home
autumn.text: Born in autumn, you like an orderly home where everything has its place and the year has its rituals: harvest dinners, end-of-year cleanups, traditions. A messy partner tests you. Pick two areas that must stay tidy and let the rest go.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Autumn at home: two tidy zones, peace everywhere else.

winter.heading: Your season at home
winter.text: Born in winter, you want home to be a den: warm, quiet, safe from the world. You recharge there. A social partner may fill it with people; agree on how often, so your den stays yours too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter at home: a warm den. Agree how often guests visit.

earth.heading: Your season at home
earth.text: Born in the Earth days, you're the household's steadying presence through changes: moves, new jobs, babies, renovations. You make transitions feel manageable. Make sure your partner takes the lead on some of them, so you're not always the one holding it all together.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Earth-days at home: steady in changes. Share the lifting.

peer.heading: What you bring to the two of you
peer.text: Your chart's most common element is your own, so what you bring is self-possession: you stay yourself inside the relationship and expect your partner to stay themselves too. That keeps the couple from turning into one blurry person. Offer closeness as freely as independence, so they don't mistake your self-sufficiency for distance.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You bring self-possession. Offer closeness just as freely.

output.heading: What you bring to the two of you
output.text: Your chart's most common element is your output, so what you bring is expression: affection, humor, creativity, the little gestures that make a relationship feel alive. You make love visible. Save some of that sparkle for ordinary weekdays, not only special occasions.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You bring sparkle. Spend some of it on a Tuesday.

wealth.heading: What you bring to the two of you
wealth.text: Your chart's most common element is your wealth element, so what you bring is practicality: a well-run home, plans that happen, problems solved. Your partner can rely on you completely. Mix in unstructured time together, where nothing needs to be achieved.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You bring a well-run life. Add unstructured time.

power.heading: What you bring to the two of you
power.text: Your chart's most common element is your power element, so what you bring is commitment: integrity, responsibility, promises kept. Your partner never has to wonder if you'll show up. Let them see your playful side too; reliability is even more lovable with a sense of humor.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You bring commitment. Show the playful side as well.

resource.heading: What you bring to the two of you
resource.text: Your chart's most common element is your resource element, so what you bring is understanding: patience, insight, a calm presence. You're good at seeing your partner's inner world. Speak up about yours as well, so understanding flows both ways.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You bring understanding. Let them understand you too.

output.heading: What to borrow from each other
output.text: Your chart is short on its output element, expression, so the thing worth borrowing from your partner is their way of saying what they feel. Watch how they do it and copy one habit: a nightly 'best part of today', a text when they miss you, a compliment said out loud.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Borrow their way of saying feelings out loud.

wealth.heading: What to borrow from each other
wealth.text: Your chart is short on its wealth element, initiative and planning, so the thing worth borrowing is your partner's drive to make things happen. Let them pull you into plans, and take the lead on one shared project a year yourself.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Borrow their drive. Then lead one project yourself.

power.heading: What to borrow from each other
power.text: Your chart is short on its power element, structure, so the thing worth borrowing is your partner's reliability habits: calendars, routines, keeping small promises. It makes the relationship feel safe for both of you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Borrow their routines. Safety lives in small promises.

resource.heading: What to borrow from each other
resource.text: Your chart is short on its resource element, support and comfort, so the thing worth borrowing is your partner's ability to rest and be looked after. Let them show you how to slow down.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Borrow their rest. Let them teach you slow mornings.

none.heading: What to borrow from each other
none.text: With all five elements in your chart, you can adapt to almost any partner. The thing worth borrowing is their certainty about what they want. Let their clarity help you name your own preferences more often.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Borrow their certainty. Name your preferences more.

gap-wood.text:
You never ask for reassurance, so they assume you don't need it. You do. The sentence that lands deepest for you: "I've got this one. You can rest."

Yeon: Being told you're strong just adds weight. You've heard it your whole life.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for relief by name. "Can you take this one?"

gap-wood.heading: The sentence you need to hear

eul-wood.text:
You adjust to everyone, so the sentence that melts you is: "What do YOU want?" Asked like they actually want the answer.

Yeon: You'll say "I don't mind". They should ask again. You do mind.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: "What do you want?" Asked twice. That's your love language.

eul-wood.heading: The sentence you need to hear

byeong-fire.text:
You light up everyone, so the line you need is: "I see how much you give." Not thanks for the party. Recognition of the effort under it.

Yeon: You'll act like you don't need it. You'll replay it for a month.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You need to be noticed noticing. Ask for that.

byeong-fire.heading: The sentence you need to hear

jeong-fire.text:
You give quiet, close attention, so you need it back in the same size: "I remembered." The small detail. The thing you mentioned once in March.

Yeon: A grand gesture won't move you half as much as them knowing your order.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Small remembered things are your proof of love.

jeong-fire.heading: The sentence you need to hear

mu-earth.text:
You hold everything up, so the sentence you need is: "You don't have to hold it all." Said while they actually take something off your plate.

Yeon: Words without the plate thing don't count. You'll notice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Mountains need a day off too. Ask for one.

mu-earth.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gi-earth.text:
You look after everyone, so what you need is to be looked after back. "Sit. I'll do it." Tea you didn't make. A plan you didn't organise.

Yeon: You'll try to help them help you. Don't. Sit.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Sit down. Let the tea be made for you. Once.

gi-earth.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gyeong-metal.text:
You protect everyone, so the line that gets you is: "I'm on your side." Out loud, especially when you were the one being difficult.

Yeon: You'll pretend it doesn't affect you. Your shoulders will drop two inches.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Swords want loyalty, not compliments. Ask for loyalty.

gyeong-metal.heading: The sentence you need to hear

sin-metal.text:
You hold yourself to impossible standards, so you need: "You don't have to get it right with me." Permission to be messy and still adored.

Yeon: You'll argue with it. Let them say it anyway.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to be unpolished with your person.

sin-metal.heading: The sentence you need to hear

im-water.text:
You need room, so the line you need is: "Go. I'll be here." Freedom that doesn't come with a guilt trip.

Yeon: Give you space without sulking, and you'll come back faster than anyone expects.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hold an ocean loosely and it keeps coming back.

im-water.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gye-water.text:
You feel everything and say little, so what you need is: "Tell me. I won't rush you." Patience for the slow version of your feelings.

Yeon: Push you and you'll say "nothing". Wait, and you'll say everything.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rain needs time to soak in. Ask for that time.

gye-water.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gap-wood.text:
On a date, Gap Wood plans. You booked the table, checked the weather, and know a backup bar in case the first is full. It's genuinely romantic, and it can also feel like a schedule. The best dates for you are ones where you hand over control: a surprise picnic you didn't organize, a partner saying 'just get in the car.' Growth for a pine in love is letting someone else choose the direction for an evening.

As a couple, your sweet spot is doing something side by side: a hike with a goal, a class you take together, building a bookshelf with too many screws. You bond best shoulder to shoulder, working toward something visible. Keep one shared project going at all times.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Hand over one evening. Let someone else steer the pine.

gap-wood.heading: You two on a date

eul-wood.text:
On a date, Eul Wood notices everything: the lighting, the music, whether your partner's chair wobbles. You make ordinary places feel special by pointing out what's beautiful about them. Your ideal date is small and pretty, a flower market, a tiny café, a walk with no destination, and you'll remember the details for years.

As a couple, you grow best through shared rituals rather than big events. The same Sunday bakery. The song you always play in the car. Vines climb by repetition, and so does your love. If your partner prefers grand gestures, meet in the middle: let them plan the big trip, and you supply the small rituals that make it feel like yours.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same bakery every Sunday. Vines climb by repetition, so does love.

eul-wood.heading: You two on a date

byeong-fire.text:
On a date, Byeong Fire is the entertainment. You talk to the waiter, invent a game about the other diners, and suggest a second location before dessert. Partners rarely get bored. They do sometimes get tired. Your best dates have one quiet stretch built in: the walk home, a bench, ten minutes with no plan where your partner can catch up and talk.

As a couple, you shine as hosts. Dinners with friends, birthdays you throw, a home that's always full. That's real joy for you and can be a lot for a quieter partner. Agree on a ratio, say two social weekends for one at home, so the sun and the sky both get their turn.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Build a quiet stretch into every date. Ten minutes, no plan.

byeong-fire.heading: You two on a date

jeong-fire.text:
On a date, Jeong Fire wants atmosphere. Candlelight, a corner table, a conversation that goes somewhere real. You're happiest when the evening becomes a memory: the night you talked until the café closed, the song in the taxi. Loud clubs and big group dinners don't count as dates to you. They're events.

As a couple, you need regular one-on-one time that isn't about logistics. A weekly evening where the phones go in a drawer and you ask each other real questions. 'What's been on your mind?' is a whole date for you. If your partner is more of an action person, alternate: their night out, your night in. The candle burns best in a still room.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One evening a week, phones in a drawer, real questions.

jeong-fire.heading: You two on a date

mu-earth.text:
On a date, Mu Earth is steady and generous. You'll drive, you'll pay attention, you'll remember the dish they liked last time and order it. Your ideal date is unhurried: a long dinner, a slow walk, nowhere to be. Rushed dates with three venues stress you, though you'll go along to be nice.

As a couple, you build security, and security is your love letter. The savings plan, the fixed weekend routine, the home that feels like a base. Your partner might need surprises too. Schedule them if spontaneity feels unnatural: one unplanned day a month where you agree to say yes to whatever comes up. Mountains can host a festival. They just like to know the date.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One unplanned day a month. Mountains can host a festival too.

mu-earth.heading: You two on a date

gi-earth.text:
On a date, Gi Earth cares for the other person without noticing it. You check if they're cold, share your food, and ask about their mother's knee. Your ideal date involves food made with love: cooking together, a market, a homemade picnic. Fancy restaurants are fine. A meal you both made is better.

As a couple, you build home faster than most. Within months there's a shared shelf, a favorite mug, a weekly dinner. The risk is that every date becomes a domestic one. Leave the house sometimes: a weekend away, a concert, an evening where nobody needs feeding. The garden is lovely. It also enjoys seeing a new landscape.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leave the house sometimes. The garden likes new landscapes too.

gi-earth.heading: You two on a date

gyeong-metal.text:
On a date, Gyeong Metal is decisive. You pick the place, make the call, and handle the problem when the reservation is lost. Partners feel safe with you. Your ideal date has an activity with a bit of challenge in it: climbing, an escape room, a competitive board game you plan to win.

As a couple, you show love by protecting and improving: fixing the bike, sorting the bills, standing up for your partner at a family dinner. Remember that improvement can sound like criticism. Before suggesting how they could do something better, check whether they wanted help. 'Want my two cents or just my company?' saves a sword many unnecessary cuts.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: 'Two cents or just company?' Ask before improving anything.

gyeong-metal.heading: You two on a date

sin-metal.text:
On a date, Sin Metal curates. The right restaurant, the right outfit, the right playlist for the drive. Your taste is a gift, and partners usually feel lucky to be shown around your world.
