Your ideal date is beautiful and a little exclusive: a gallery opening, a rooftop, a perfect dish you read about.

As a couple, you need appreciation for the effort behind the polish. A partner who notices you planned everything is gold. One who shrugs might get a very cool evening. Tell them it matters to you. And sometimes let a date be ugly: rain, takeaway, a cheap film. Laughing through a ruined plan together is one of the best bonds a jewel can find.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Let one date go wrong on purpose. Laugh through it together.

sin-metal.heading: You two on a date

im-water.text:
On a date, Im Water wants to go somewhere new. A neighborhood you haven't explored, a train to a random town, a dish neither of you can pronounce. Routine dates feel like a tide pool to you. Your ideal date ends with a conversation that keeps going past midnight.

As a couple, you grow through adventure and ideas: travel, learning, big plans for the future. A homebody partner can feel left behind. Bring them along at their pace, and stay home with them sometimes with a curious mind. A home evening can be an adventure if you treat it like one: a new recipe, a documentary, a question you've never asked each other.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Unknown streets, unpronounceable food, talk past midnight. Your ideal.

im-water.heading: You two on a date

gye-water.text:
On a date, Gye Water is playful and perceptive. You notice your partner's mood before they mention it and adjust the evening without a word: quieter café, earlier night, extra dessert. Your ideal date is cozy with a little magic in it, a film in the rain, a late-night snack run, a secret spot you found.

As a couple, you bond through private worlds. Inside jokes, nicknames, a shared show nobody else watches. Those small worlds are precious. Make sure the big conversations happen too: plans, money, the future. They can feel heavy to rain, but having them early keeps the cozy world safe from surprises.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Inside jokes are precious. Have the big talks too, early.

gye-water.heading: You two on a date

strong.heading: How you apologize
strong.text:
A strong chart apologizes the way it does everything: firmly, once, and preferably with a plan. 'You're right, I was wrong, here's what I'll do differently.' That's a good apology, and it can still miss. Partners sometimes need the feeling before the fix. They want to know you felt the hurt, not just that you've solved it.

So slow down by one sentence. Before the plan, say what you think it was like for them. 'You were waiting and felt like you didn't matter.' Then pause. Let them correct you if needed. The fix lands softer once they feel understood. And watch the follow-up: a strong chart can say sorry and then, ten minutes later, defend itself again. Let the apology stand on its own for one evening.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Feeling before fix. One sentence about how it felt for them.

weak.heading: How you apologize
weak.text:
A weak chart apologizes too much and too fast. Sorry for the fight, sorry for being upset, sorry for something that wasn't your fault, mostly to make the bad feeling stop. Partners stop hearing it, and the real issue never gets discussed.

Try a two-part rule. Apologize only for what you actually did. Then say what you need, too: 'I'm sorry I snapped. I was hurt that you canceled again.' Both sentences matter. And when your partner apologizes, accept it fully instead of saying 'it's fine, it's nothing.' If it hurt, it wasn't nothing. Letting an apology be received is how trust gets rebuilt from both sides.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Own your part, then name your need. Two halves of one apology.

wood.heading: A home ritual that balances you
wood.text: The element that steadies your chart is Wood, the growing one. At home, that becomes a ritual of growth you share: a plant you're both keeping alive, a course you do side by side, a weekly walk in the same park watching it change through the year. Wood also likes plans. Once a season, sit down together with a notebook and write three things you want to try as a couple. Cross them off slowly. The point isn't the list. It's the feeling that you're both still going somewhere.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Once a season: a notebook and three things to try together.

fire.heading: A home ritual that balances you
fire.text: The element that steadies your chart is Fire, the warm one. At home, that becomes a ritual of warmth and light: a candle at dinner, music on while you cook, a monthly evening where you invite friends over even if the flat is messy. Fire also means celebration. Mark small wins out loud: a finished project, a good week, the first coffee on the balcony after winter. Couples who celebrate small things tend to argue less about big ones, because there's warmth in the bank.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Celebrate small wins out loud. Warmth in the bank.

earth.heading: A home ritual that balances you
earth.text: The element that steadies your chart is Earth, the grounding one. At home, that becomes a ritual of routine and nourishment: the same breakfast every Saturday, a shared grocery run, a Sunday evening reset where you tidy for twenty minutes and plan the week together. It sounds unromantic. It isn't. Predictable time together is the soil a relationship grows in, and your chart in particular relaxes when the ground is steady. Guard the routine even in busy weeks.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A Sunday reset: twenty minutes tidying, ten minutes planning.

metal.heading: A home ritual that balances you
metal.text: The element that steadies your chart is Metal, the clarifying one. At home, that becomes a ritual of clearing: once a month, a short check-in where each of you names one thing that's working and one thing to change. Keep it to fifteen minutes, keep it kind, and end with something nice. Metal also likes order, so clear one shelf, one drawer or one obligation together each month. A tidy space and a clear conversation do the same thing for you: they cut the noise.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monthly fifteen minutes: one thing working, one to change.

water.heading: A home ritual that balances you
water.text: The element that steadies your chart is Water, the reflective one. At home, that becomes a ritual of slow conversation: a late tea, a bath with the door open, a walk by the river where you talk about things that aren't logistics. Water also likes rest, so protect one completely lazy morning a week. No plans, no chores, just drifting together. Many couples skip this because it looks like doing nothing. For your chart, it's how the well refills.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One lazy morning a week, together. The well refills there.

peer.heading: A Sunday with the two of you
peer.text: Your partner shares your element, so a Sunday together runs on the same clock. You both want the long breakfast, or you both want the early run, and nobody has to negotiate. That ease is lovely and it can turn into a rut: the same café, the same show, the same walk for two years. Once a month, let one of you pick something the other would never choose. Same-element couples refresh through small surprises, not big changes, and a Sunday that breaks the pattern gives you both something new to talk about over Monday dinner.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same clock, same café. Once a month, pick something odd.

output.heading: A Sunday with the two of you
output.text: Your element feeds theirs, so on a Sunday you're often the one making it nice: the plan, the brunch, the playlist. They enjoy it and bloom. The trap is that you end the weekend tired and they end it refreshed. Swap roles every other Sunday. Let them decide where you go and what you eat, even if the result is a strange museum and cold noodles. Being on the receiving end of their effort tells you something about how they love, and it lets your own well fill up before the week starts.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Every other Sunday, they plan. Even if it's cold noodles.

wealth.heading: A Sunday with the two of you
wealth.text: Your element shapes theirs, so on a Sunday you tend to steer: what time to leave, which errands, which friends. They often like being steered, and the day runs smoothly. Make sure it's also their day. Ask one open question in the morning, 'What would make today good for you?', and build around the answer. Steering is a gift when it serves both people. When it only follows your list, they'll start saving their real wishes for days without you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask them first thing what a good day looks like. Build from there.

power.heading: A Sunday with the two of you
power.text: Their element shapes yours, so on a Sunday they often set the pace and you adapt. That can feel safe, and some weeks it's exactly what you want. Other weeks you'll notice you haven't done one thing you chose. Claim a slot: a morning, an afternoon, two hours that are yours to decide, out loud and in advance. Partners with a shaping element usually respect a clear request far more than a quiet sulk, and they're often relieved to be told what you actually want.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Claim two hours out loud, in advance. They'll respect it.

resource.heading: A Sunday with the two of you
resource.text: Their element feeds yours, so a Sunday with them usually means being looked after. A cooked breakfast, a plan that's already made, a sofa that's already warm. Enjoy it. Then give something back in your own currency, which doesn't have to match theirs: fix the thing they mentioned, plan next weekend, take them somewhere they've wanted to go. Couples where one element feeds the other stay sweet when the receiver says thank you in actions, not only words.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Being looked after is lovely. Say thanks in actions.

new.speaker: bom
new.text: Under a year. Still in the part where you learn how they take their coffee and what their silence means.

settled.speaker: yeon
settled.text: One to three years. The honeymoon left, the real people moved in. This is where it gets interesting.

long.speaker: bom
long.text: Three-plus years. You can read their mood from the sound of the keys in the door.

committed.speaker: yeon
committed.text: Engaged or married. So you've signed up for the long version. Let's make sure you both read the manual.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: You didn't say how long. Doesn't matter. Whether it's month two or year ten, the patterns are already there.

time.speaker: yeon
time.text: You fight about time and attention. Translation: one of you is saying "I miss you" in the angriest possible way.

logistics.speaker: yeon
logistics.text: Chores, plans, money stuff. Nobody's really fighting about the dishes. Nobody has ever really fought about the dishes.

feelings.speaker: bom
feelings.text: Feelings and communication. So you both care enough to argue about how you talk. That's actually a good sign.

people.speaker: yeon
people.text: Friends or family. Ah. The fight where you're both defending someone who isn't even in the room.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: You skipped what you fight about. Maybe you don't fight much. Or maybe it's the thing nobody says.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

sin-metal.how-you-love:
You love with precision. The right words, the right gesture, the right moment. It means so much to you.

Bom: And when they get it wrong, it stings sharper than it should.

Yeon: One careless comment and you're cold for a day. They have no idea why.

Bom: Tell them what landed wrong, gently, while it's small. They want to get you right.
sin-metal.how-you-fight:
Sin Metal goes cool and precise when hurt. Your tone sharpens, your replies get short, and your partner feels frozen out without knowing why. You can also hold grudges quietly. Name what hurt, specifically and kindly. 'When you said that in front of your friends, it embarrassed me.' Your precision is a gift; use it for feelings.

You also remember exact words. Months later you can quote what was said, which makes your partner feel like they're on trial. Let some things fade. Keeping the receipts protects you for a while and then poisons the well.

You repair through thoughtful gestures: a careful note, a beautiful apology, a small gift that shows you understood. Lovely, and even better when paired with a plain 'I was wrong about that.'
sin-metal.growing-together:
To Sin Metal, growing together means refining: becoming better versions of yourselves together, creating a beautiful shared life, developing good taste as a couple. You thrive with a partner who appreciates quality and puts effort into the details. Couples grow with you when both people keep polishing.

You also grow by appreciating each other out loud. You notice details others miss, so say what you notice: the way they handled their mother, the effort they put into dinner. Polishing a relationship is mostly attention, and you have plenty of it.
sin-metal.long-term:
Year after year, Sin Metal is a thoughtful, loyal partner who keeps romance elegant. The risk over decades is perfectionism: expecting the relationship to always look and feel right. Real love has scratches. Let some imperfection be part of the story.

Your long-term gift is a relationship that stays refined, respectful and considerate. Your long-term lesson is gentleness with flaws, yours and theirs. Twenty years in, the scratches are the story.

sin-metal.speaker: bom
sin-metal.text: The jewel in love. Thoughtful, refined, the partner who remembers the exact gift.

sin-metal.speaker: yeon
sin-metal.text: Also noticed the gift they got YOU was from the airport. Silently. Forever.

sin-metal.speaker: bom
sin-metal.text: You love with care and taste. You want every moment between you to feel considered.

sin-metal.speaker: yeon
sin-metal.text: Going cold isn't a message. Name the hurt.

sin-metal.speaker: bom
sin-metal.text: You two keep polishing. That's growth for you.

sin-metal.speaker: yeon
sin-metal.text: Real love has scratches. Let it.

spring.intro: A jewel born in spring. Everything was growing and you noticed all of it: what's pretty, what's off, what's three millimetres crooked. You have taste. You also have opinions about other people's taste.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You judged the font on their birthday card. Silently.

summer.intro: A jewel in summer heat. Pressure shaped you: to look good, do well, never be the embarrassing one. You're polished and impressive. One careless comment can still ruin your whole week.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to be unfinished. It's charming, honestly.

earth.intro: A jewel still in the earth. Born in the soil weeks, so you were protected, maybe a little over-protected. You need to feel safe before you sparkle, and that's not a flaw. It's quality control.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You need three green flags before one selfie.

autumn.intro: A jewel born in metal's own season. Double shine. High standards, sharp eye, zero patience for sloppy. You're the friend people dress up for. You're also the friend people are slightly scared to disappoint.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're a five-star review. With a long comment section.

winter.intro: A jewel in winter water, washed clear. Your mind is quick and your words are precise. You can say one sentence that fixes everything, or one that ends everything. Most of the time you know which.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You see people so clearly. Use it to be kind.

sin-metal.strong:
Your chart is strong, which in a relationship means a firm sense of self, clear opinions and the energy to carry a lot. You're a stable partner and a confident one. The blind spot is pushing: deciding for both of you, arguing until you win, assuming your way of doing home, money or holidays is the obvious one. The best couples with a chart like yours have explicit agreements, made together and revisited.

Sin Metal with this much support has exacting standards. Make sure they're shared, not imposed.
sin-metal.weak:
Your chart is the weak kind, which in a relationship means sensitivity, adaptability and a deep capacity for empathy. You're attuned to your partner in ways they may not even notice. The blind spot is giving too much: adjusting to their needs, swallowing your preferences, avoiding conflict until resentment builds. The best couples with a chart like yours have a partner who asks what you want and waits for the answer.

Sin Metal on a lighter chart feels every careless word. Choose a partner who's gentle with yours.

sin-metal.title: Your gift was perfect. Theirs was from the airport. You noticed.
sin-metal.text:
You put thought into everything: the restaurant, the card, the words. You want love to feel beautiful and intentional.

Bom: You make them feel precious.

Yeon: You also grade them. Quietly. On a curve they've never seen.
sin-metal.end: Yeon: And the thing you actually need from them isn't on the rubric. Next page.

cliff.sin-metal: Yeon: Now, who you're with, Jewel. They love you in ways that | aren't polished, and you've been marking them down for it.

sin-metal.speaker: yeon
sin-metal.text: Growing together means letting them be clumsy at loving you. Clumsy and trying beats polished and gone.
